These predicates have completely different meanings and roles in the domain. They represent different aspects of the world – one about a state of being (having breakfast) and the other about location. Merging them would create a complex and potentially ambiguous predicate, violating rule (2) which discourages overly general predicates. The predicates are not semantically equivalent, and they have distinct uses in the domain. The relationship between them is not a containment relationship.
